correctness.rationale: Exact formula (1) counts specified off-path and endpoint leaves via rooted-forest deletion: denominator k*n^(m-1), numerator (k-s)*(n-r-s)^(m-1), with zero impossible boundary. The two-variable binomial transform gives the full conditional PGF. Direct subtraction yields (7) with a single sign change and the specified terminal step; the cubic-root optimum follows. A uniform expansion for d<=n^(3/5) plus Rayleigh/Gaussian distance tails establishes (5) and moment convergence for (6). A separately executable standard-library Prüfer enumerator passed 3013 tests, exhausting all labeled trees of size 3..8 and checking finite algebra to size 74. No finite check is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The known Joyal correspondence maps cyclic vertices of uniform mappings to a marked-tree path and mapping indegree-zero vertices to the off-path leaves. Thus the entire off-path marginal (the s=0 moment family), and its leading distance covariance, are already covered by existing mapping conditional-moment results: these are expressly excluded from the new contribution. The non-covered and mathematically distinctive claim is the mixed off-path/marked-endpoint leaf law (s=1,2), its full total-leaf conditional PGF, and the sharp nonmonotone conditional mean with cube-root optimizer. The previously indexed endpoint-degree theorem also lacks those joint moments. Historical multivariate enumeration could implicitly contain them, a stated risk.
residual_risks: Older multivariate labeled-tree generating-function literature may imply (1) without matching the search wording, especially historical Cayley-tree parametrization work.
Some historically plausible enumerative papers do not have inspectable full text; no claim of absolute uniqueness or independent novelty certification.
General rooted-forest counting is classical and excluded from novelty; the claimed contribution is the joint specialization and sharp dependent asymptotics.
The off-path-only subcase is explicitly covered by previously known mapping moments under Joyal, so only the coupled endpoint law and optimized total-leaf regression carry an originality claim.

value.rationale: The number of leaves and marked-vertex separation are natural global/geometric statistics. Although Joyal’s mapping correspondence already yields the off-path leaf marginal, combining it with the two path-endpoint leaf indicators produces a complete joint law and a sharp, nonmonotone optimum at separation order n^(1/3), contrasting with typical n^(1/2) separation and the monotone local-degree regression. This structural crossover is the principal value, not the already-covered off-path-only moment family or leading covariance.
